title: consul 1.19.0 breaks all tags
body: After upgrading from Consul 1.18.2 to 1.19.0, DNS tag lookups stopped filtering services. Any string placed to the left of a service name resolves successfully and returns the same pool as the untagged name. This broke my primary and standby PostgreSQL lookups because both names returned all hosts. Downgrading to 1.18.2 made tagged lookups work again.

symptoms_visible: On Consul 1.19.0, arbitrary names such as tags.are.definitely.borked.consul.service resolve to the same three hosts as the untagged consul.service name.
My primary and standby PostgreSQL DNS names both return hosts from the full pool.
After downgrading to 1.18.2, tagged lookups work again.
N0.label: N0 DNS tag regression reported

symptoms_visible: On another affected deployment, the service-hosting servers show Consul 1.19.1, but querying master.13-pgcluster01.service.consul-dev still returns all three service addresses.
N1_x.label: N1_x apparent persistence after partial 1.19.1 update

symptoms_visible: The tag has no periods, and master.13-pgcluster01.service.consul-dev still returns 10.0.1.168, 10.0.1.170, and 10.0.1.169.
N2.label: N2 tag syntax and query output collected

symptoms_visible: The tagged lookup still returns all three addresses while the service-hosting servers are on Consul 1.19.1 and the DNS resolver agents are still on the older version.
N3.label: N3 queried DNS agents found on older version

symptoms_visible: On my dev deployment, tagged DNS lookups work correctly after I update the DNS resolver agents as well as the service-hosting servers.
N_terminal.label: terminal second affected deployment verified

symptoms_visible: On the second affected deployment, tagged DNS lookups work correctly once every agent serving the DNS request is updated.
N_terminal_shortcut.label: terminal shortcut with affected-operator confirmation

solution.intent: Install Consul 1.19.1 only on the servers hosting the registered service and assume that is sufficient to correct tagged DNS lookups.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade the servers hosting the service to Consul 1.19.1, then retry the tagged name.

edges.comment: Issue c8 and c13, different affected operator explicitly folded into the simulated user side: the service-hosting servers were on 1.19.1, but the DNS resolvers were not, so updating only those servers did not change the observed DNS response.

question_patterns: Does the affected tag itself contain any periods or multiple dot-separated components?
What is the exact tag text before the service name?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No, there are no periods in the tag. The name I am querying is master.13-pgcluster01.service.consul-dev.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Yes, the tag is this.is.my.tag and the simple tag master works correctly.
The tag is primary rather than master, but it also contains no periods.

question_patterns: Can you share the exact DNS command and its raw output from the affected deployment?
What addresses are returned for the tagged service name?

edges.comment: Issue c9-c10, participant4's separate dev deployment folded explicitly: the maintainer asked about periods in the tag, and the affected operator answered with the exact tag and query output. The attachment belongs to this raw-output clarification.

question_patterns: Which Consul agent actually receives this DNS query, and what version is that agent running?
Are the client agents or DNS resolver agents receiving the query on the same version as the service-hosting servers?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The servers hosting the service were running 1.19.1, but my DNS resolvers were not.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The DNS query goes directly to a resolver confirmed to be running 1.19.1, and every Consul client and server in the deployment is also on 1.19.1.
Two resolver agents were still on the earlier version rather than just one.
The resolver hosts use a different Linux distribution from the service hosts.

edges.comment: Issue c11-c13, participant4's separate dev deployment: maintainers asked whether the DNS request was hitting a client agent or another server and whether every agent being queried was on 1.19.1. The operator then checked and reported that the DNS resolvers had not been updated. This version check changes knowledge but not system state.

solution.intent: Treat the original behavior as the Consul 1.19.0 tagged-DNS regression addressed by the linked fix, and ensure every Consul agent that can receive or serve the DNS query—including client-side DNS resolvers—is updated to 1.19.1 before retesting.
solution.concrete_example: The UI version of a service-hosting server does not establish the version of the agent answering port 8600 DNS requests. Check the queried client or resolver agents, update those agents to 1.19.1 too, and rerun the same tagged lookup to verify that it returns only matching instances.
solution.inference_hint: The affected operator supplied only the deployment-version facts: service-hosting servers were on 1.19.1 while DNS resolvers were not. Concluding that the apparent 1.19.1 failure came from an older agent actually serving the DNS request is the engineer-side inference. The linked PR's internal mechanism is not described in this issue and must not be invented.

edges.comment: Issue c11-c16: after discovering that the DNS resolver agents had not been updated, participant4 updated them and reported that everything worked. This final observation is confirmation from a different affected operator, not a retest by the opening reporter.

solution.intent: Deploy the tagged-DNS fix by updating every Consul agent that can answer DNS requests, including resolver and client agents, then verify the tagged lookup rather than updating only service-hosting servers.
solution.concrete_example: Move all agents serving Consul DNS off 1.19.0 and onto 1.19.1, including any client or resolver reached by the DNS request, then repeat the primary or master tagged query and confirm that only tagged instances are returned.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut encodes the correct first response: update the agents actually serving DNS, not merely the servers visible in the UI. The issue does not describe the linked PR's implementation details, so the diagnosis must remain at the tagged-DNS regression and mixed-version deployment level.

edges.comment: Shortcut answer derived from c1 and c11-c13. The successful observation comes from participant4's separate affected dev deployment; the opening reporter never posted a personal retest after the fixed release.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the original fault as a Consul 1.19.0 DNS tag-lookup regression: arbitrary or mismatched tag prefixes return the unfiltered service pool, while downgrading to 1.18.2 restores filtering.

Must ground the apparent continued failure after updating in the collected deployment evidence: the service-hosting servers were on 1.19.1, but the Consul DNS resolver agents receiving the query were not.
Must recommend updating every Consul agent that can serve the DNS request, including client or resolver agents, rather than treating an update of only the service-hosting servers as sufficient.
Must not invent the internal mechanism of the linked fix because the issue only states that a linked PR resolves the regression.
Must ask for the original tagged lookup to be repeated after all relevant DNS-serving agents are updated before declaring that deployment resolved.
Must preserve verification provenance: a second affected operator confirmed success after updating the resolvers, but the opening reporter did not report a personal retest.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Consul operator comfortable with DNS queries, SRV records, cluster upgrades, configuration details, and diagnosing production-impacting service-discovery behavior; a second affected dev-cluster operator is explicitly folded into the user side for the later 1.19.1 verification.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and operationally focused, with concrete command output and strong concern about outage risk; cooperative when maintainers request exact tag syntax, query output, and agent-version details.
